Rashi on Ketubot 16a:10:1.hebrew: בשלמא לר' אלעזר דאמר - בפרק קמא, טענתייהו במנה ולא כלום. מוכת עץ שלא הכיר בה אינה יכולה לתובעו אלא מנה, והוא אומר: "דרוסת איש את ואין ליך כלום" — איכא מגו, דאי בעיא אמרה: "מוכת עץ אני תחתיך":
Rashi on Ketubot 16a:10:1.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Elazar, who said - in the first chapter [that] their dispute [is about] a maneh versus nothing: [a woman whose hymen was] ruptured by wood whom he did not recognize can claim from him only a maneh, while he says, "You were deflowered by a man, and you have nothing." [Here] there is a miggo, for if she wanted, she could have said, "I am [one whose hymen was] ruptured by wood under your [authority]."

Rashi on Ketubot 16a:10:2.hebrew: וקאמרה - מוכת עץ אני מעיקרא, ולא תבעה אלא מנה, מהימנא:
Rashi on Ketubot 16a:10:2.english: And she says - "I am [one] ruptured by wood from before [betrothal]," and she claims only a maneh [one hundred dinars] — she is believed.

Rashi on Ketubot 16a:10:3.hebrew: אלא לר' יוחנן - דאמר טענתייהו במאתי' ומנה, שהיא תובעתו מאתים, ליכא מידי בין תחתיו למעיקרא; מאי מגו איכא:
Rashi on Ketubot 16a:10:3.english: However, according to Rabbi Yoḥanan - who says their dispute is over two hundred [dinars] and one hundred [dinars], as she is claiming two hundred from him — there is no difference between [being ruptured] under him and [being ruptured] initially; what miggo is there?

Rashi on Ketubot 16a:11:1.hebrew: משארסתני - אירע לי ונסתחפה שדהו, ואית לי מאתים:
Rashi on Ketubot 16a:11:1.english: After you betrothed me - [it] happened to me, and his field was inundated, and I am entitled to two hundred [zuz].

Rashi on Ketubot 16a:13:1.hebrew: הכא - גבי שדה, אין שור שחוט לפניך שיעלה על לב בעליו לתבוע מי שחטו; כלומר, אם שתק זה, לא היו לו עוררים. הלכך, אי לאו דדבר פשוט הוא שלקחה הימנו, לא היה אומר לו "של אביך היתה", הלכך אמרי' מגו. אבל גבי לא מצא לה בתולים, שור שחוט לפניך — בתולים שלא מצא לה הם הסיתוהו לבא לב"ד; ואע"פ שיש לה להשיב טענה טובה מזו, לא אמרינן מגו, דדלמא לא אסקה אדעתה, א"נ איערומי קא מערמא:
Rashi on Ketubot 16a:13:1.english: Here - Regarding the field, there is no slaughtered ox before you such that it would occur to its owner to sue [and ask] who slaughtered it; that is to say, if this [occupant] had remained silent, he would have had no challengers. Therefore, were it not a clear matter that he purchased it from him, he would not have said to him, "It belonged to your father"; therefore, we apply miggo. However, regarding [the case where] he did not find her [to have] signs of virginity, there is a slaughtered ox before you: the signs of virginity that he did not find in her are what prompted him to come to court. Even though she could have replied with a better claim than this, we do not apply miggo, because perhaps it did not occur to her, or alternatively, she is acting craftily.

Rashi on Ketubot 16a:14:1.english: And since most women - This is a question.

Rashi on Ketubot 16a:14:2.english: She has publicity - And many [people] know that she went out in a hinuma [bridal veil].

Rashi on Ketubot 16a:1:1.hebrew: שהפה שאסר - זה אינו יודע שהיתה של אביו אלא על פיו של זה, ומה שאסר הרי התיר:
Rashi on Ketubot 16a:1:1.english: For the mouth that prohibited - This [claimant] does not know that it belonged to his father except through this [possessor]'s mouth, and what he prohibited, he has permitted.

Rashi on Ketubot 16a:2:1.english: The reason is that there are witnesses - That she went out with a hinnuma.

Rashi on Ketubot 16a:2:2.hebrew: הבעל מהימן - ולא אמרינן, הואיל ומספקא לן על יום נישואיה אם בתולה היתה אם בעולה, העמד אותה על חזקתה של קודם לכן, ומתחלה בתולה היתה:
Rashi on Ketubot 16a:2:2.english: The husband is deemed credible - And we do not say [that] since we are in doubt regarding the day of her marriage whether she was a virgin or a non-virgin, establish her on her prior presumptive status, and originally she was a virgin.

Rashi on Ketubot 16a:2:3.english: She is deemed credible - For he follows the presumption of the body.

Rashi on Ketubot 16a:3:1.hebrew: בברי ושמא - גבי משארסתני נאנסתי, היא טוענת ברי לי הוא, והוא אינו טוען אלא שמא עד שלא ארסתיך, דהא אינו יודע מתי נאנסה:
Rashi on Ketubot 16a:3:1.english: In [a case of] a certain [claim] and an uncertain [claim] - Regarding [the case of a woman who says,] "After you betrothed me, I was violated": she claims, "It is certain to me," whereas he only claims, "Perhaps [it happened] before I betrothed you," since he does not know when she was violated.

Rashi on Ketubot 16a:4:1.english: And he who asked it - [meaning] to say [that the] anonymous [Mishnah] is not in accordance with Rabban Gamliel.

Rashi on Ketubot 16a:4:2.hebrew: מאי קארי לה - ומאי עלה בדעתו לאפוקי מדר"ג? הא לא דמיא לה:
Rashi on Ketubot 16a:4:2.english: Why did he ask it - And what entered his mind to exclude [this case] from [the ruling of] Rabban Gamliel? Behold, it is not similar to it.

Rashi on Ketubot 16a:4:3.hebrew: כיון דרוב נשים בתולות נישאות - קרובה טענתה להיות אמת יותר משלו, וכברי ושמא דמיא:
Rashi on Ketubot 16a:4:3.english: Since most women are married [as] virgins - Her claim is closer to being true than his, and it is like [a case of] a certain [claim] and an uncertain [claim].

Rashi on Ketubot 16a:5:1.hebrew: והכי נמי מסתברא - דר"ג מודה בה דבעל מהימן:
Rashi on Ketubot 16a:5:1.english: And it also stands to reason - that Rabban Gamliel concedes in this [case] that the husband is believed.

Rashi on Ketubot 16a:5:2.hebrew: אי אמרת בשלמא איירי ר"ג במודה - דהך רישא הודאה הוא דקא מודה ר"ג לרבי יהושע, ואמר: אע"ג דפליגנא עלך בברי ושמא, מודינא לך בברי וברי — היינו דשייך למיתני בתריה: "ור' יהושע מודה לר"ג בהאומר לחברו שדה זו כו'", דאע"ג דפליגנא בפ"ק ב"משארסתני נאנסתי", דאע"ג דאיכא למימר מגו לא מהימנא, מודינא בהאי מגו, דאי בעי שתיק ולא א"ל "של אביך היתה", כי אמר ליה נמי "לקחתיה הימנו" מהימן, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Ketubot 16a:5:2.english: Granted, if you say that Rabban Gamliel is dealing with conceding - That this first clause [of the Mishnah] is a concession that Rabban Gamliel makes to Rabbi Yehoshua, saying, "Even though I disagree with you in [a case of] a certain [claim] and an uncertain [claim], I concede to you in [a case of] a certain [claim] and a certain [claim]" — that is why it is appropriate to teach after it: "And Rabbi Yehoshua concedes to Rabban Gamliel regarding one who says to his fellow, 'This field,' etc."; [meaning:] even though I disagreed [with you] in the first chapter regarding [the case of,] "After you betrothed me I was violated," [holding] that even though one could argue *migo*, she is not believed, I concede regarding this *migo*, that since if he wanted he could have remained silent and not said to him, "It was your father's," when he also says to him, "I bought it from him," he is believed, as [explained] below.

Rashi on Ketubot 16a:5:3.hebrew: אלא אי אמרת לא איירי - רישא במודה ר"ג, מאי "מודה רבי יהושע"? מאי שייך למיתנייה הכא, ואהיכא קאי:
Rashi on Ketubot 16a:5:3.english: But if you say [it] does not deal - [if] the first clause [does not deal] with Rabban Gamliel conceding, what [is meant by] "Rabbi Yehoshua concedes"? What relevance is there to teach it here, and to what does it refer?

Rashi on Ketubot 16a:6:1.hebrew: אמגו קאי - אפלוגתא דאיכא למימר בה מגו בפ' קמא קאי, וקאמר: אע"ג דפליגנא במגו דהתם, במגו דהכא מודינא, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Ketubot 16a:6:1.english: It is in reference to miggo - It refers to the dispute in which miggo can be argued in the first chapter, and [Rabbi Yehoshua] is saying: Even though I disagree regarding the miggo there, regarding the miggo here I agree, as [will be explained] below.

Rashi on Ketubot 16a:7:2.english: Her belly is between her teeth - And she cannot say, "I have not engaged in intercourse."

Rashi on Ketubot 16a:8:1.english: And she says: I engaged in intercourse - [Meaning:] and I engaged in intercourse with a fit [man], she is deemed credible.

Tosafot on Ketubot 16a:13:1.hebrew: התם שור שחוט לפניך - פירש בקונטרס: שהוא טוען "עד שלא אירסתיך נאנסת", והכא אין שור שחוט לפניך, דאין הלה תובעו. ור"י מפרש דהכא נמי איירי בהלה תובעו, כדפי'. וה"פ: התם שור שחוט לפניך, דהרי אין לה בתולים, ואינה יכולה לומר "בתולה אני", כמו בשור שחוט שאין יכול לומר "חי הוא"; ולהכי, בין אומרת "משארסתני נאנסתי" בין אומרת "מוכת עץ אני תחתיך", לא מהימנא. הכא אין שור שחוט לפניך, ונאמן במגו דאי בעי אמר "לא היתה של אביך מעולם":
Tosafot on Ketubot 16a:13:1.english: There, [there is] a slaughtered ox before you - [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres that [the husband] claims, "Before I betrothed you, you were raped," and here there is no slaughtered ox before you because the other party [i.e., the son] is not suing him. And R"I explains that here too [the Gemara] is speaking of [a case] where the other party is suing him, as I explained [above]. And this is its explanation: There, [there is] a slaughtered ox before you, for behold, she has no signs of virginity, and she cannot say, "I am a virgin," just like with a slaughtered ox where one cannot say, "It is alive"; and therefore, whether she says, "After you betrothed me I was raped," or she says, "I was struck by wood while [betrothed] to you," she is not believed. Here, [there is] no slaughtered ox before you, and he is believed with a miggo, for if he wanted, he could have said, "It never belonged to your father."

Tosafot on Ketubot 16a:14:1.hebrew: כיון דרוב נשים בתולות נישאות כי ליכא עדים מאי הוי - לרב פריך, דאית ליה הולכין בממון אחר הרוב:
Tosafot on Ketubot 16a:14:1.english: "Since most women are married as virgins, if there are no witnesses, what of it?" - [The Gemara] raises an objection against Rav, who holds [that] we follow the majority in monetary [matters].

Tosafot on Ketubot 16a:2:1.hebrew: דאי רבן גמליאל הא אמר איהי מהימנא - נראה דלמ"ד הטוען אחר מעשה ב"ד לא אמר כלום פריך; דלמ"ד דמצי טעין "פרעתי", הכא נאמן הבעל אפילו לר"ג לומר "אלמנה נשאתיך", במגו דאי בעי אמר "פרעתי":
Tosafot on Ketubot 16a:2:1.english: As, if [it were] Rabban Gamliel, didn't he say [that] she is deemed credible? - It appears that [the Gemara] is asking according to the one who says [that] one who makes a claim against an act of the court has said nothing; for according to the one who says that he can claim, "I have paid," here the husband is deemed credible even according to Rabban Gamliel to say, "I married you [as] a widow," with a migo that if he wanted, he could have said, "I have paid."

Tosafot on Ketubot 16a:5:1.hebrew: הכי נמי מסתברא - פי' בקונטרס: "הכי נמי מסתברא", דמתני' אתיא כרבן גמליאל כדמשנינן דבברי וברי מודה, מדקתני "ומודה ר' יהושע" כו'. וקשה לפי': דכי לא איירי נמי ר"ג במודה, אתי שפיר "ומודה רבי יהושע" — כלומר, אע"ג דברישא פליגנא עלך, בסיפא מודינא לך — אע"ג דרישא וסיפא אינן מענין אחד; כי היכי דאתיא ליה שפיר "ומודה רבי יהושע" אי איירי ר"ג במודה, אע"ג דמודה דר' גמליאל אינו מענין ומודה דרבי יהושע! ויש ליישב: דודאי כי איירי ר"ג במודה, שייך למיתני שפיר "ומודה רבי יהושע", אע"ג דלא הוי מענין אחד — כלומר, דאגב דתנא מילתא דמודה ר"ג, תני נמי מילתא דמודה בה רבי יהושע; אבל אי לא איירי רבן גמליאל במודה, לא שייך למיתני "ומודה רבי יהושע" לאשמועינן אע"ג דפליג ברישא מודה בסיפא, כיון דרישא וסיפא אינם מענין אחד. אבל קשה: דלא הוה ליה למימר "אמגו קאי", דעד השתא נמי לפ"ה אמגו הוי קאי. ונראה לר"י דה"פ: "הכי נמי מסתברא" דכברי ושמא דמי, ולא בא לומר דפליג רבן גמליאל ברישא, אלא אע"ג דכברי ושמא דמי מודה ר"ג, משום דלאו שמא ממש הוא, מדקאמר "ומודה רבי יהושע". "אי אמרת בשלמא איירי ר"ג במודה" — כלומר, אע"ג דכברי ושמא דמי, מודה ר"ג דבעל נאמן — היינו דקתני "ומודה רבי יהושע" דבהאי ברי נאמן, דס"ד דטעמא דרבי יהושע משום ברי ושמא, דזה אינו תובעו כדפי' בקונט'; והשתא הוה מודה דר"ג ומודה דר"י מענין אחד. "אלא אי אמרת" דרישא בברי וברי גמור הוא ולא איירי רבן גמליאל במודה — דפשיטא דכיון דברי וברי הוא דלא פליג ר"ג — מאי "ומודה"? וקאמר: "מי סברת" דארישא קאי וטעמא דר"י משום ברי ושמא? "אמגו קאי", דטעמא דר' יהושע משום מגו, ונאמן אפי' הלה תובעו, "ואפירקין קמא קאי":
Tosafot on Ketubot 16a:5:1.english: It also stands to reason - Rashi explained: "It also stands to reason" that our Mishnah accords with Rabban Gamliel, as we answered [earlier] that in [a case of] a certain [claim] and a certain [claim] he concedes, since [the Mishnah] teaches, "And R. Yehoshua concedes," etc. And it is difficult according to his explanation: for even if Rabban Gamliel is not speaking of conceding, "And R. Yehoshua concedes" still works well — meaning, "Even though in the first clause I disagree with you, in the latter clause I concede to you" — even though the first clause and the latter clause are not of the same topic, just as "And R. Yehoshua concedes" works well for him if Rabban Gamliel is speaking of conceding, even though Rabban Gamliel's concession is not of the same topic as R. Yehoshua's concession! One can resolve [this]: certainly, when Rabban Gamliel is speaking of conceding, it is appropriate to teach "And R. Yehoshua concedes," even though it is not of the same topic — that is, since [the Tanna] taught a case where Rabban Gamliel concedes, he also teaches a case where R. Yehoshua concedes; whereas if Rabban Gamliel is not speaking of conceding, it is not appropriate to teach "And R. Yehoshua concedes" to inform us that although he disagrees in the first clause he concedes in the latter clause, since the first clause and the latter clause are not of the same topic. However, [there is still] a difficulty: [the Gemara] should not have said [later], "It refers to miggo," for until now as well, according to Rashi's explanation, it already referred to miggo! Rather, it appears to Ri [R. Yitzchak] that this is its explanation: "It also stands to reason" that it is like [a case of] a certain [claim] and an uncertain [claim]; and [the Gemara] does not mean to say that Rabban Gamliel disagrees in the first clause, but rather that even though it is like a certain [claim] and an uncertain [claim], Rabban Gamliel concedes because it is not truly an uncertain [claim], [as is proven] from that which it states, "And R. Yehoshua concedes." "Granted, if you say that Rabban Gamliel is speaking of conceding" — that is, even though it is like a certain [claim] and an uncertain [claim], Rabban Gamliel concedes that the husband is believed — that is why it teaches "And R. Yehoshua concedes" that in this certain [claim] he is believed, for it might have entered your mind that R. Yehoshua's reason is because of a certain [claim] and an uncertain [claim], since this [claimant] does not claim against him, as Rashi explained; and now Rabban Gamliel's concession and R. Yehoshua's concession are of the same topic. "But if you say" that the first clause is a case of full certain [claim] and certain [claim] and Rabban Gamliel is not speaking of conceding — for it is obvious that since it is a certain [claim] and a certain [claim] Rabban Gamliel does not disagree — what is "And [R. Yehoshua] concedes"? And [the Gemara] says: "Do you think" that it refers to the first clause and R. Yehoshua's reason is because of a certain [claim] and an uncertain [claim]? "It refers to miggo," for R. Yehoshua's reason is because of miggo, and he is believed even if the other party claims against him, "and it refers to the first chapter."
